:::{#def-extended-nonneg-reals}
#### Extended non-negative real numbers

The **extended non-negative real numbers**, written $[0, \infty]$,
are the non-negative real numbers together with an extra element $\infty$
that is greater than every real number:

$$[0, \infty] \eqdef [0, \infty) \cup \set{\infty}$$

Addition extends to $[0, \infty]$ by setting

$$
\begin{aligned}
x + \infty &= \infty + x \\
&= \infty
\end{aligned}
$$

for every $x \in [0, \infty]$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-infinity-arithmetic}
#### Arithmetic with $\infty$

$\infty$ is not a real number,
so some real-number arithmetic does not extend to it:
$\infty - \infty$ is left undefined,
and $\infty + 1 = \infty + 2$ does not imply $1 = 2$.
Measure theory uses $[0, \infty]$
because the size of a set, such as the length of the whole real line, can be infinite
[@wikipedia_extended_real_number_line].

:::
